_comment: Per-plugin settings for run_tests.py. Plugins not listed here still get route discovery, the unauthenticated probe and the source checks; enabling MCP and authenticated calls are skipped.
enable_php: run with 'wp --user=admin eval' to switch MCP on (as an admin would in the settings UI). {token} is replaced with a random secret generated for the run.
endpoint: path under /wp-json/ (or a full URL). Omit to pick one from the discovered routes.
enable_php may echo 'token:<value>' (e.g. a key made with the plugin's own create-key function); that value then replaces {token} in auth.
enable_php may be "" when the endpoint is on as soon as the plugin is activated. It can also create the credential the auth block uses.
auth.type: basic (admin application password, created per run) | header (auth.name: auth.value) | bearer (auth.value) | none | oauth (OAuth only: AUTH is left to the manual sheet).
transport: external when the MCP server runs outside WordPress (npm package or hosted relay): EN, A3 and AUTH are recorded as N/A.
notes: shown in the report, e.g. design decisions that explain a probe result.

public_by_design: the source code shows the endpoint is deliberately public (e.g. permission_callback __return_true with a comment saying why). Tools returned without credentials then do not count as a hard fail. Quote the evidence (file:line) in public_evidence.

mcp-for-woocommerce.public_evidence: includes/Core/McpStreamableTransport.php:58-61: permission_callback __return_true, commented 'Intentionally public: every tool returns only storefront data a visitor can already see, nothing is written'
mcp-for-woocommerce.notes: Endpoint is public by design; source says tools only return storefront data.

royal-mcp.notes: API key is bound to a user (api_key_user_id). Activating via WP-CLI binds it to user 0, so the config binds it to admin.

ai-engine.notes: Access requires manage_options; also supports a bearer token and OAuth.

vibe-ai.notes: Relays MCP through the hosted wpvibe.ai service using an application password; no MCP route on the site.

easy-mcp-ai.notes: On by default. Per-token tool allow-lists; also OAuth and a URL-embedded key route.

miniorange-secure-mcp-server.notes: On by default; the endpoint only accepts OAuth bearer tokens.

wsp-mcp-ai-agents-connector.notes: Endpoint on by default with 6 read tools; the rest are off by default. Config switches every ability on. Accepts application passwords, a plugin API key or OAuth.

cowboy-mcp.notes: On by default ('enabled' => true at activation). API keys always act as the first administrator. Exposes 2 meta-tools (cowboy_discover, cowboy_run) that route to the real tools, so tool count and name-based breadth undercount: judge breadth manually.

alphabridge-mcp.notes: Tokens are bound to a user and scope (default full). Write access has a separate main switch, off by default.

aicom.notes: Route is open; the router checks scoped API keys. Key created with every scope.

stifli-flex-mcp.notes: On by default. OAuth 2.1 or application passwords; legacy SSE route too.

agent-abilities-for-mcp.notes: Endpoint on by default but every tool is off until enabled (aafm_enabled_abilities, includes/registry.php). Config enables every registered ability; high-risk ones stay locked by the plugin's own floor.

diviops-agent.notes: MCP server is the separate @diviops/mcp-server npm package; the plugin adds REST endpoints it calls with an application password.

ai-workflow-automation-ai-agent-hub.notes: On by default (MCP Adapter). OAuth 2.1, JWT or application passwords.

nibwp.notes: Off by default: master switch nibwp_ai_abilities_enabled, locked to the domain it was enabled on (includes/helpers.php nibwp_is_enabled; same two options as nibwp_relock_domain). Exposes the MCP Adapter's 3 meta-tools; run_tests counts the abilities behind them via discover-abilities.

mountdev-ai-mcp-connector.notes: On by default. OAuth for Claude/ChatGPT, application passwords for editors.

iato-mcp.notes: On by default. Application passwords, OAuth, or a plugin-generated bearer key.

invizo-mcp.enable_php: $s = new Invizo_MCP_Settings(); $m = new ReflectionMethod($s, 'get_allowed_scope_options'); $m->setAccessible(true); update_option('invizo_mcp_settings', $s->sanitize(array('enabled' => 1, 'allowed_scopes' => array_keys($m->invoke($s)))));
invizo-mcp.notes: Off by default ('enabled' => false, no scopes). Config enables the endpoint and every available scope. Packaging bug: v2.0.8 from WordPress.org ships without vendor/, so the bundled MCP Adapter is missing and /mcp/invizo never registers; config installs the MCP Adapter plugin to work around it. Exposes the Adapter's 3 meta-tools; run_tests counts the abilities behind them via discover-abilities.

ylabs-ai-assistant-connector.notes: Adds wp-agent/v1 REST endpoints for an external assistant that authenticates with application passwords; no MCP endpoint on the site.

abilities-bridge.notes: Endpoint on by default; the route is open and the server checks OAuth bearer tokens or application passwords. Abilities API bridge and memory are off by default; config turns both on. Each ability still needs admin approval, so the tool count is what you get before approving any.

acadium-agent-publisher.notes: On by default. Readme documents OAuth 2.1 only, but an application password works.

albert-ai-butler.notes: On by default. OAuth 2.0 only: an application password gets 403 (changelog: app-password access to the tools was closed deliberately).

devcubic-ai-bridge-for-mcp.notes: On by default. OAuth 2.1 only: an application password gets 401 'A valid access token is required.'

publishio.notes: On by default (MCP Adapter server). Readme documents OAuth, but an application password works.

rectus-content-access-for-mcp.notes: Uses the MCP Adapter default server. Readme documents OAuth 2.1, but an application password works. Exposes the Adapter's 3 meta-tools; run_tests counts the abilities behind them via discover-abilities.

saddle.notes: On by default. OAuth or application passwords (readme: each key works only with Saddle).

siteskite.notes: Off by default: siteskite_mcp_enabled, pinned to the host it was enabled on (includes/Mcp/McpSettings.php). Site MCP works without a SiteSkite account. An application password passes the endpoint check but tools/list is refused (403) until an AI app is connected via OAuth or a SiteSkite API key, so treat as OAuth only.

strifebridge-mcp.notes: On by default but needs a token: OAuth 2.1 or the legacy token in sbmcp_api_token (stored in plain text). An application password gets 403.

track-debug.notes: On by default. Application passwords via the WordPress MCP proxy. 6 generic tools (list-content, save-content, batch...), so name-based breadth undercounts.

webo-mcp.notes: On by default. Application passwords or a logged-in session; optional API key / HMAC as an extra gate.

sokket-site-connector-for-mcp.enable_php: $s = get_option('sokket_settings', []); if (!is_array($s)) { $s = []; } $s['enabled'] = true; update_option('sokket_settings', $s); $r = new \SOKKET\Tools\Registry(); $k = (new \SOKKET\Auth\TokenManager())->create('run_tests', 1, array_keys($r->get_tools()), false); echo is_array($k) ? 'token:' . $k['token'] : 'error';
sokket-site-connector-for-mcp.notes: Off by default (sokket_settings enabled => false, 503 until on). Bearer tokens are bound to a user with a per-token tool list; config allows every tool. OAuth is a separate opt-in.

bcs-mcp-manager.notes: Off by default (bcs_mcp_settings enabled, 503 'MCP server is disabled.' until on). Readme documents OAuth 2.0 only. An application password gets 401.

counterhand-mcp-for-woocommerce.notes: Off by default (counterhand_settings enabled, src/Features/McpServer/McpServerFeature.php). Pretty /mcp URL plus a REST fallback; the route is open and process() returns 401 without an OAuth 2.1 token. OAuth only (CIMD consent flow).

admindra-mcp.notes: Needs the separate MCP Adapter plugin (readme Installation step 2; no Requires Plugins header). Bundles an OAuth server that requires HTTPS, so OAuth cannot complete on a plain-http Studio site. Content edits off by default (admindra_mcp_content_edits).

acrossai-mcp-manager.notes: Off by default: both seeded servers have is_enabled = 0 (wp_acrossai_mcp_servers). Config enables the recommended AcrossAI server, whose toolset needs the companion plugin acrossai-abilities-manager (the quick-connect wizard installs it). Bundles the MCP Adapter. OAuth, application passwords, CLI or WP-CLI STDIO. The recommended server exposes 14 grouped toolset tools, so the tool count undercounts.
